subject.title: fix(embeddings): bound openai-compatible requests without AbortSignal

question: Should unsignaled OpenAI-compatible embedding calls adopt hard 60-second query and 120-second batch request ceilings for all supported remote and self-hosted endpoints?
rationale: The code correctly prevents indefinite hangs, but selecting a universal hard cutoff changes existing behavior and may reject valid slow local-model requests; repository policy cannot determine the acceptable compatibility tradeoff without provider-owner intent.

options.title: Calibrate before merge
options.body: Confirm representative slow self-hosted query and batch behavior, then raise or otherwise adjust the fixed ceilings if 60/120 seconds rejects supported workloads.

options.title: Accept the fixed ceilings
options.body: Land the 60/120-second defaults as the supported unsignaled policy and explicitly accept that slower requests must provide a caller-owned signal budget.

options.title: Move policy to callers
options.body: Keep the transport generic and require gateway, capability CLI, and other entry points to install their own operation-specific deadlines.

recommendation.title: Calibrate before merge
recommendation.body: Confirm representative slow self-hosted query and batch behavior, then raise or otherwise adjust the fixed ceilings if 60/120 seconds rejects supported workloads.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged embedding-runtime refactors make this the strongest available owner signal for deciding the shared provider timeout contract.
